decisionsTitle: The ship says whether production answered, and a stopped release can be re-labelled (amending §426, §535)
decisionsSection:
**Context (2026-10-03).** The release of `BR-V2.65` from the phone waited 59 minutes 35 seconds in ship's production wait while the club's domain was on a registrar hold. The log said «waiting for BR-V2.65-2026-10-03 on production», then «STOP: production never reported BR-V2.65-2026-10-03» — the same two lines it prints when production answers with another build. `health()` swallowed the fetch error and returned an empty body, so ship itself could not tell the cases apart. Then the run's closing comment and the removal of the `ship` label were refused («Resource not accessible by personal access token»): the label stayed on, and adding it again could start nothing. Both cost the owner an evening.

**Decision.**

- **One reading, judged.** `scripts/ship-checks.mjs` gains `judgeProductionReading({ body, error }, expected)`, pure and tested, returning one of four kinds: `no-answer` (a fetch error, described by its cause — «TypeError fetch failed — ENOTFOUND <host>: a name or network failure», a refused connection, a certificate (Node's `CERT_*`, `ERR_TLS_*`, `UNABLE_TO_*`, `DEPTH_ZERO_*` codes), a timeout), `other-build` (the body names another baseline), `expected`, and `unreadable` (an empty body or an HTML page: a hold or parking page, a proxy's error). `health()` in `scripts/ship.mjs` returns `{ body, error, status }` instead of an empty string.
- **The waits say what they see.** Both production waits (step 1 for the previous baseline, step 7 for the new one) run through `waitForProduction`. It prints on the first reading and then every two minutes, not on every 20- or 30-second poll. The three readings in its words:
  - «no answer for 12 min: TypeError fetch failed — ENOTFOUND <host>: a name or network failure; docs/RUNBOOKS.md § The domain stops answering»;
  - «production answers with BR-V2.64-…; waiting for BR-V2.65-…»;
  - «production answers but its body carries no baseline (HTTP 200, no baseline in the body)».
- **The STOP names the case.** «production never reported <baseline> — <the last line>» and «production did not report <baseline> in time — <the last line>», with «check Vercel's production deployment» added when another build answers. The STOP's first line is the times file's `outcome`, so the summary page's table says it too. The PR comment also carries it: «The release stopped (failure) — ship: <outcome> — …», cut to 600 characters inside `jq`, never by bytes, so «—» and «§» are never split. The final «production: …» line is unchanged.
- **Where «no answer» sends the reader.** The no-answer line names `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § The domain stops answering, a new section: does the name resolve, is the domain on a registrar hold or expired, does Vercel's **Domains** page say «Valid Configuration», is the certificate issued. Its last line says what follows when the domain answers again.
- **After a STOP, two different next steps.** Step 1's STOP («never reported <previous>») comes before anything merged: tick **ship** again once production answers. Step 7's («did not report <new> in time») comes after the pull request and the `qa → main` release merged: a second run would take its starting baseline from `main` and find nothing to propose to `main`, stopping with a second «The release stopped» for a release that went out. So the label is not ticked again: no answer means the domain triage, another build means fixing or redeploying Vercel's production deployment, and the release is done once `/api/health` reports the new baseline. `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § When it stops and `docs/DISPATCHER.md` § Ship say both.
- **The comment and the label use the job's own token.** `release.yml`'s `permissions` gain `pull-requests: write` and `issues: write`. The step «Say so on the pull request» runs with `GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}`. A comment or a label changed by GitHub's token starts no workflow, which is right: only a person adding the label must start a release. Every push, merge and approval keeps `SHIP_TOKEN`, because what GitHub's token pushes or merges starts no workflow (§535). `contents` stays `read`. The label comes off through the REST call (`gh api -X DELETE …/issues/<PR>/labels/ship`), not `gh pr edit`, which also reads the pull request's projects, more than the job's token is granted. The label comes off only in a run the label started; a run started by hand has none to remove. The token no longer needs **Issues** (`SETUP.md` § 41); a token that has it may keep it.

**Refused.**
- A shorter wait. The hour at the start and the twenty minutes at the end are right for a deploy that is slow; what was missing was the words, not a shorter clock.
- A retry of the label by the workflow itself. After a STOP, a person decides what to do next, as above; the workflow never re-labels or restarts itself.

**Amends §426 and §535 (2026-10-03).** §426's ship gains a judged production reading next to its judged checks. §535's «Say so on the pull request» writes with the job's token, and the job's permissions are no longer read-only. `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § Release from the phone, its new § The domain stops answering, and `docs/DISPATCHER.md` § Ship say what the log says now and what to do in each case.
changelogLine: - **The release says whether production answered** — while it waits for production, ship prints every two minutes whether the site did not answer (with the network error), answers with another build, or answers with a page that carries no baseline, and its STOP, the summary page and the pull request's comment name the case; the comment and the `ship` label's removal now use the run's own token, so a stopped release can be labelled again. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given `yarn ship`, when it waits for production to report a baseline, then it judges each reading as no answer (naming the fetch error's cause), another build (naming its baseline), the expected one, or a body with no baseline. It prints what it sees on the first reading and then every two minutes, and its STOP names the same case; a no-answer line names `docs/RUNBOOKS.md` § The domain stops answering, a section that exists, and a TLS failure code (`CERT_*`, `ERR_TLS_*`, `UNABLE_TO_*`, `DEPTH_ZERO_*`) reads as a certificate failure. Given `.github/workflows/release.yml`, the closing comment carries that STOP cut to 600 characters (never bytes), and the comment and the label's removal run with the job's own token, which may write pull requests and issues; every push, merge and approval runs with `SHIP_TOKEN`. Verification: unit `scripts/ship-checks.test.ts`, `scripts/release-workflow.test.ts` (2026-10-03, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the release says whether production answered, and a stopped release can be labelled again
